messages:
anna: Heads-up — after the 1950 deploy we saw a p99 jump on the small-realtime model. p50/p95 steady, p99 moved from ~120ms to ~480ms. Not seeing obvious CPU/GPU saturation.

mike: Can you paste profiler breakdown? sounds like tail-surge not overall throughput.

anna: Putting the short flame summary here. This is from a 5m sample of live traffic (prod):

```text
decode_stage_total_ms: 420
  kernel_exec_ms: 220
  kv_lookup_ms: 90  (miss-rate 11.8%)
  scheduling_wait_ms: 110
prefill_stage_total_ms: 60
  prefill_kv_lookup_ms: 8 (miss-rate 2.1%)
```

anna: Two notes: (1) prefill is still cheap, (2) decode has a larger scheduling_wait and KV miss contribution during tails. Looking like microbatch scheduling + KV churn.

kai: Interesting. Which scheduler settings are live? max_microbatch=16, max_wait_ms=40?

anna: Correct. Config snippet:

```json
{"microbatch": {"max_size": 16, "max_wait_ms": 40, "aggressive_batching": true}, "kernel_pick": "auto"}
```

sasha: If aggressive_batching is true we might be holding requests to fill batches which increases scheduling_wait for low-concurrency requests and pushes them into a different kernel path. Could explain p99 but not p95.

len: Another angle: kernel auto-selection changed in 0.9.2 to prefer fused-attn kernels for decode which have different memory/KV access patterns. If KV cache misses rise, decode latency jumps. Did we upgrade kernels in the deploy?

anna: Yes — runtime bumped kernel selector to 0.9.2 heuristics in this deploy. Reverting selector to prior behavior is one quick experiment.

mike: For a controlled test: create two canaries with identical traffic split. Canary A: kernel_selector=0.9.1 + microbatch.max_size=8. Canary B: current (0.9.2, max_size=16). Compare p95/p99 and KV miss rates over 30m. I'll run the job.

kai: Also try turning off aggressive_batching on a canary — that reduces scheduling_wait but costs throughput; good to quantify unit-cost delta.

anna: Agreed. Also planning lower-level profiling to see whether kv_lookup_ms is remote (RDMA) vs local LRU miss path. I saw more network KV calls in logs for decode.

sasha: If KV is remote, batching could amplify cache churn (many requests bumping different keys). We should sample per-request key distribution near tails.

len: Quick patch idea: prefer a kernel that keeps a small pinned KV window for active sessions (sticky cache) during decode-heavy workloads. Might reduce misses but costs memory. Worth an A/B.

mike: Tests scheduled now:
- canary-1: kernel_selector=0.9.1, microbatch.max_size=8, aggressive_batching=false
- canary-2: kernel_selector=0.9.2, microbatch.max_size=16, aggressive_batching=true (prod)
Collect metrics: p50/p95/p99, kv_miss_rate, scheduling_wait_ms, tokens/s, cost-per-token. 30m baseline + 2h extended.

anna: Added notes to the experiment ticket: link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-8261 (private)

deploy-bot: Rollout 1950 -> canary completed. 10% traffic to canary-1, 10% to canary-2.

mike: Early 30m snapshot: canary-1 p99=140ms, canary-2 p99=490ms. KV miss rate: canary-1=3.2%, canary-2=11.6%. scheduling_wait_ms median: c1=20ms, c2=95ms.

anna: That's pretty decisive. Looks like 0.9.2 selector + larger microbatches amplify tail via KV misses + waiting.

kai: Action items:
- Rollback kernel_selector heuristics to 0.9.1 by default (sasha + infra) — short-term.
- Run a dedicated KV locality experiment (len) to try sticky cache for active sessions.
- Add a runtime flag to prefer smaller microbatches for low-concurrency routes (mike).
- Instrument per-request key distribution near tail (anna).

sasha: I'll open the rollback PR now, will target hotfix branch and metric-check gating.

len: I'll prototype sticky-KV patch but will need perf knobs to cap memory.

anna: Also let's add an automatic fallback: if kv_miss_rate > 8% and p99 > 200ms, switch decode kernel to fallback path that favors KV localism. Quick circuit-breaker to reduce customer impact.

mike: Will add an alert for kv_miss_rate > 8% AND p99 > 250ms to trigger paging.

anna: Thanks all. I'll update the incident doc and link CI+bench results once rollback lands. :thumbsup:

len: Great. Small note — longer term we should evaluate microbatching policies that are workload-aware (e.g., size by session token affinity) not just by time/size thresholds. Could get best of both worlds.

anna: Yep. Captured in backlog under INF-8270. Closing this thread for now while we run the rollback and experiments.
